subject: Information Theory
title: Arithmetic Coding
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Arithmetic Coding.

hook.text: Huffman assigns whole bits per symbol. What if one deserves 0.3 bits? Arithmetic coding handles fractions.

buildup.text: Instead of coding one symbol at a time, arithmetic coding encodes the entire message as one number.

discovery.text: It subdivides the interval [0,1) based on symbol probabilities. The final number encodes the full message.

twist.text: Arithmetic coding can beat Huffman by approaching entropy more closely—especially for skewed distributions.

climax.text: It's used in H.264 video, JPEG 2000, and modern file compressors where every fraction of a bit matters.

punchline.text: One number encodes the whole message.

quiz.question: What advantage does arithmetic coding have over Huffman?
options: It can approach entropy more closely using fractional bits
